h1: Linear DNA µg to pmol of Ends Converter
summary:
A linear DNA molecule has two ends, and many reactions care about the number of ends rather than the number of molecules — ligation, biotin labelling, exonuclease chewing. It returns molecules, mass, ends and ends per microgram, and the panel shows all of them at once.

One microgram of a 1 kb fragment is 1.5 pmol of molecules but 3 pmol of ends, and this calculator gives both without the arithmetic. The arithmetic keeps full precision internally and only rounds what it displays, so the number you copy out is the number the formula produced. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Linear DNA µg to pmol of Ends Converter
sections.html:
pmol of molecules = µg × 10⁶ ÷ (660 × length). pmol of ends = 2 × pmol of molecules. Ends per µg = 2 × 10⁶ ÷ (660 × length)

The symbols in the formula

sections.title: How do I use the Linear DNA µg to pmol of Ends Converter?
sections.html:
Fill the boxes you have numbers for; the calculator decides what it can derive from them.

  1. Enter the length of the fragment in base pairs and the mass in micrograms.
  2. The molar amount and the number of ends are both reported.
  3. If you know how many pmol of ends you need, type it and the mass is solved instead.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: length of 1,000 bp.

Substituting them into the formula gives molecules of 1.52 pmol, mass of 1 µg, ends of 3.03 pmol, ends per microgram of 3.03 pmol/µg, molecules of 912,445,569,697.

Because the example uses the defaults, you can reproduce it by loading the page and reading the results panel before touching anything.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
Interpretation is a convention, not part of the arithmetic. The usual bands are:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
under 200 bpMany ends per µg0.5 µg of a 100 bp fragment carries 15 pmol of ends
200 – 3 000 bpTypical cloning fragment1–7 pmol of ends per microgram
over 10 000 bpFew endsa microgram carries well under 1 pmol of ends

  • Ligations are driven by the concentration of ends, not the mass of DNA: two fragments of different lengths at equal mass do not have equal numbers of ends.

  • A circular plasmid has no ends, which is why a dephosphorylated vector is measured in molecules and an insert in ends.

  • Below about 1 nM of ends, the two termini rarely meet and the ligation stalls however much enzyme you add.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
Before blaming the formula, check these — they explain nearly every mismatch:

  • Using the molecules figure where the ends figure belongs — the answer is out by exactly 2.
  • Applying this to a circular molecule, which has no ends at all.
  • Forgetting that the mass must be the whole molecule, not the insert length.

faq.q: Why do ends matter more than molecules?
faq.a: Every ligation event joins two ends, so the rate depends on how often a 5′ and a 3′ terminus meet.

faq.q: How many pmol of ends are in 1 µg of a 500 bp fragment?

faq.a: No. A closed circle contributes no ends, so it cannot ligate to anything without being cut first.

faq.q: What does the Linear DNA µg to pmol of Ends Converter actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns molecules, mass, ends and ends per microgram. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
